name: Dynamic Programming Fundamentals
explanation: Dynamic Programming solves complex optimization problems by breaking them down into overlapping subproblems and storing subproblem results (memoization/tabulation).
learning_objectives: Identify optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems
common_misconceptions: Confusing Dynamic Programming with Greedy choices
Failing to define base cases causing recursion stack overflow or out-of-bound array access

no_hint.message: Your state transition logic is coming together nicely. Keep tracking subproblem dependencies.
no_hint.next_step: Verify that your base cases cover the smallest possible inputs.
no_hint.reflection_question: What is the value of your DP state at index 0 and index 1?

concept.message: Dynamic Programming avoids recomputing subproblems by storing calculated results in a table (DP array or dictionary).
concept.next_step: Define what dp[i] represents in plain words before writing code.
concept.reflection_question: How does storing the result of subproblem i help compute subproblem i + 1?

guided.message: Establish base cases dp[0] and dp[1]. Then iterate from index 2 to N using state recurrence dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2].
guided.next_step: Set up an array of size N + 1 initialized with base values.
guided.reflection_question: Which previously computed DP values are needed to compute the current step?

pseudocode.message:
dp = ARRAY OF SIZE N + 1
dp[0] = base_case_0
dp[1] = base_case_1
FOR i FROM 2 TO N:
    dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2]
RETURN dp[N]
pseudocode.next_step: Translate the iterative DP table logic into your language.
pseudocode.reflection_question: Can you optimize the space complexity by storing only the last two variables instead of a full array?

full_solution.message: By filling a DP table iteratively using state transition dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2], we achieve O(N) time and O(N) space (optimizable to O(1) space).
full_solution.next_step: Refactor your solution to use two variables to achieve O(1) auxiliary space.
full_solution.reflection_question: Why is the top-down memoization approach functionally equivalent to bottom-up tabulation?

reflection_questions: What is the recurrence relation connecting dp[i] to smaller subproblems?
pseudocode:
dp[0] = 1, dp[1] = 1
FOR i = 2 UNTIL N:
    dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2]
RETURN dp[N]

complexity.time: O(N) - Linear pass through DP state table
